statement: (i) Prove that $\frac{1+\tan\theta}{1-\tan\theta}=\tan\!\left(\theta+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$. (ii) Hence solve $\frac{1+\tan\theta}{1-\tan\theta}=2$ for $0\le\theta<\frac{\pi}{2}$. (iii) Show that the equation in (ii) has no solution in $(\frac{\pi}{2},\pi)$.
solution: (i) $\tan(\theta+\frac{\pi}{4})=\frac{\tan\theta+1}{1-\tan\theta}$. (ii) $\tan(\theta+\frac{\pi}{4})=2\Rightarrow \theta+\frac{\pi}{4}=\arctan 2$, so $\theta=\arctan 2-\frac{\pi}{4}$ (which lies in $(0,\frac{\pi}{2})$). (iii) For $\theta\in(\frac{\pi}{2},\pi)$, $\tan\theta<0$; write $\tan\theta=-t$ with $t>0$. Then $\frac{1-t}{1+t}=2\Rightarrow 1-t=2+2t\Rightarrow -3t=1$, impossible for $t>0$. Hence no solution.
hints: Set tan theta negative in the second interval.
